NovaCore Health is a team passionate about biomedical engineering, technology, and space exploration. Our goal is to develop health monitoring software that helps astronauts understand and track their health during space missions.

We want to combine physiological data, clear visualizations, and useful alerts in an intuitive platform that supports crew health awareness. Our interests include designing technology for challenging environments.

details:
NovaCore Health – Astro Health

Project Overview

Astro Health is a medical monitoring software designed to support astronaut health and well-being during space missions. Developed by the Novacore Health team, it aims to address the challenges of monitoring human health in environments where access to immediate medical assistance is limited by the distance from Earth.

Spaceflight exposes astronauts to physiological changes that can affect multiple aspects of their health, including cardiovascular function, sleep patterns, fatigue, and vision. These changes may develop throughout a mission and require continuous attention. Astro Health seeks to organize relevant health information, identify potential anomalies, and provide useful alerts to support medical monitoring and decision-making.

Our project consists of a functional software prototype developed in Python. Its main purpose is to transform complex health information into an organized and accessible system that helps users and medical teams understand changes in astronaut health.

How Does Astro Health Work?

Astro Health works as a centralized health monitoring platform. It organizes astronaut health information into individual profiles and presents relevant data through a medical dashboard.

The general workflow consists of collecting or entering health data, organizing the information, displaying physiological parameters, identifying potential deviations, and generating alerts when certain conditions require attention.

The platform includes the following main components:

Medical Dashboard: The dashboard provides a centralized view of astronaut health information. It allows users to visualize physiological data, review health parameters, and identify changes that may require further attention. Its purpose is to make medical information easier to understand and access.

Astronaut Health Profiles: Each astronaut can have an individual health profile containing relevant medical information and health parameters. This organization allows users to review information associated with each astronaut and maintain a more structured overview of their health throughout a mission.

Physiological Monitoring: Astro Health focuses on observing relevant physiological variables and identifying changes that may indicate potential health concerns. By organizing these measurements, the platform helps users recognize variations and follow their development over time.

Medical Alert System: The software generates notifications when potential anomalies are identified in the available health data. These alerts are intended to draw attention to parameters that may require additional review by medical personnel. They serve as an early warning and decision-support mechanism, not as an independent medical diagnosis.

Neuro-Ocular Monitoring: Astro Health can incorporate specialized monitoring modules, including neuro-ocular assessment. This component addresses vision-related changes associated with spaceflight, particularly those related to Spaceflight-Associated Neuro-Ocular Syndrome (SANS). Its purpose is to support the observation and early identification of potential ocular changes that may affect astronauts during long-duration missions.

Health Trend Analysis: By organizing physiological information, the platform can help users review changes in health parameters and recognize patterns that may be relevant to medical monitoring. This can contribute to a better understanding of how an astronaut's condition evolves throughout a mission.

Checsito: A Virtual Health Companion

One of the most creative features of Astro Health is Checsito, a virtual pet inspired by the classic Tamagotchi concept.

Checsito introduces a gamification approach to health monitoring. Its appearance changes according to the user's health parameters, creating a visual representation of the astronaut's current health status.

Instead of presenting health information exclusively through numbers and charts, Checsito provides a more interactive and engaging experience. Its changing appearance encourages astronauts to pay attention to their health measurements and maintain awareness of their physiological condition.

This feature seeks to make health monitoring more approachable, encourage healthy habits, and create a stronger connection between users and their personal health information.

Checsito is designed as a motivational and educational element. It does not diagnose medical conditions or replace professional health assessments.

Benefits and Intended Impact

Astro Health aims to provide several benefits for astronaut health monitoring:

  • Centralized information: Organizes relevant medical information in one accessible platform.
  • Early identification of potential anomalies: Generates alerts that help draw attention to unusual physiological changes.
  • Improved health awareness: Makes it easier for astronauts to understand and follow their health parameters.
  • Medical decision support: Provides organized information that can assist medical teams in evaluating astronaut health.
  • Specialized monitoring: Supports the incorporation of modules addressing specific health concerns, such as neuro-ocular changes.
  • Engagement through gamification: Uses Checsito to encourage users to remain aware of their health and maintain healthy habits.

Our long-term vision is to develop Astro Health into a more comprehensive platform that can integrate additional medical monitoring modules and support the evolving healthcare needs of astronauts.

Technology and Development Tools

Astro Health was developed using Python as its primary programming language. Python was selected because of its flexibility and its suitability for developing software applications that organize, process, and visualize health-related information.

The project was developed as a functional prototype that demonstrates the main concept and intended workflow of the platform.

Its software-based architecture allows the possibility of expanding the system with additional monitoring modules, new physiological variables, and other specialized health features.

At its current stage, the prototype works with simulated and historical datasets. It does not yet have direct access to real-time astronaut telemetry or full integration with spaceflight-grade medical hardware.

Creativity and Innovation

Astro Health combines medical monitoring, physiological data visualization, specialized health modules, and gamification in a single platform.

Its main innovation is not only the organization of astronaut health information, but also the way it seeks to make that information more understandable and actionable.

The combination of a medical dashboard, individual astronaut profiles, anomaly notifications, and neuro-ocular monitoring provides a flexible approach to space health monitoring.

Additionally, Checsito introduces a human-centered element that distinguishes the project from conventional medical dashboards. By connecting health parameters with a virtual companion, the software seeks to encourage participation and continuous awareness of personal health.

The modular concept also allows Astro Health to evolve as new health monitoring requirements emerge, making it adaptable to different medical needs during space missions.

Factors Considered During Development

Our team considered several important factors when designing Astro Health:

  • Spaceflight health risks: Physiological changes associated with microgravity and long-duration missions.
  • Limited medical access: The challenges of providing timely medical assistance when astronauts are far from Earth.
  • Data accessibility: The importance of presenting medical information in a clear and organized format.
  • Early warning: The need to identify potential abnormalities that may require further medical evaluation.
  • User engagement: The importance of encouraging astronauts to remain aware of their health through interactive features.
  • Expandability: The possibility of incorporating additional medical monitoring modules as the project develops.
  • Medical reliability: The importance of distinguishing software-generated alerts from clinical diagnoses and validated medical decisions.

Current Limitations and Future Development

Although Astro Health has a functional Python prototype, further development is necessary before it can be implemented in actual space missions.

Currently, the system uses simulated and historical datasets rather than direct real-time telemetry from astronauts. Integration with spaceflight-grade sensors and medical equipment remains a future development objective.

The prototype also requires extensive testing, verification of its alert mechanisms, and formal clinical validation to evaluate its reliability and usefulness in real medical environments.

Future development could include real-time data integration, expanded physiological monitoring, additional specialized medical modules, improved trend analysis, and further development of the neuro-ocular monitoring component.

Our team recognizes that Astro Health is a decision-support tool and not a replacement for medical professionals.

Final Vision

Novacore Health believes that protecting astronaut health is essential for the future of space exploration. As missions become longer and travel farther from Earth, accessible and organized medical information will become increasingly important.

Through Astro Health, we aim to transform complex space health data into useful information, encourage health awareness, and support medical teams in monitoring astronauts throughout their missions.

NovaCore Health: Because exploring space also means protecting those who make that exploration possible.
